subject: Packaging options for Sparrow pilot — tier / feature tradeoffs
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Packaging options for Sparrow pilot — tier / feature tradeoffs

Ben / Kim — forwarding Sparrow's RFP snippet and a quick read of where they are leaning. They want a 6-week pilot across two markets and asked for guidance on: tier selection (throughput vs feature bundle), short-term discounts for pilot, and what the upgrade/downgrade path looks like if they expand or contract after the pilot.

Key context: Sparrow will ingest PHI through a consented pilot and wants predictable latency (95th < 300ms) and an option to burst. They asked for a conservative price guardrail for scaling to full production. Procurement is involved and likely to request a short-term credit if we ask for a minimum commit.

Options I'm thinking about (please weigh pros/cons):
- Option A — Throughput-first pilot (compact tier, quantized model): lower per-token cost, higher latency risk for complex prompts, easy scale to Dedicated.
- Option B — Feature-first pilot (full-feature bundle, hosted with reserved capacity): higher cost but includes function-calling and structured output guarantees; simpler for product team to evaluate capabilities.
- Option C — Hybrid: hosted compact for customer-facing endpoints + dedicated inference for batch workflows; requires routing config and a bit more ops work.

Attachments: Sparrow_RFP_v2.pdf (excerpt), initial tier-pricing-calc.xlsx (draft)

Ask: Ben — can you lead the customer-facing reply with clear pricing table and explicit upgrade / downgrade mechanics? Kim — can you review SLA / reserved capacity language and any limits on graceful downgrade (credits, proration)?

Thanks — will hop on a quick sync if useful.

— Mateo
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging options for Sparrow pilot — tier / feature tradeoffs

Hi Emma — great to meet you over email. Thanks for sending the RFP excerpt — we took a close look and sketched three concrete pilot packages so you can pick the path that best maps to your evaluation needs. Quick TL;DR: two paths (throughput vs feature) + a hybrid if you want both evaluation signals.

1) Throughput Pilot (Compact Tier) — recommended if your primary goal is transaction volume/cost benchmarking
- What you get: quantized models, automatic batching, conservative KV caching
- Latency target: 95th < 300ms typical for short prompts
- Price signal: lowest per-token unit cost, no feature add-ons
- Upgrade path: move to Dedicated pools (reserved) with a 30-day notice; any prepaid credits are applied pro-rata to reserved capacity.

2) Feature Pilot (Full Bundle) — recommended if you need to validate tool-calling, structured outputs, and fidelity
- What you get: full model variant, function/tool calling enabled, prioritized routing during pilot window
- Latency target: 95th < 350ms (depends on prompt complexity)
- Price signal: higher per-token cost + optional seat/route fees
- Upgrade path: same as above; where customers keep feature entitlements and can submit a canary rollout request.

3) Hybrid — compact hosted endpoints for public-facing traffic + Dedicated for heavy batch jobs. Slightly more ops work but best of both worlds.

Pilot discount: We normally offer a 15% pilot discount for 6-week evaluation. If Sparrow commits to a 3-month reserved capacity after pilot, we can convert unused pilot credits into commitment credits.

Attachments: tier-pricing-calc.xlsx (detailed numbers)

Next step: Would you be available for a 30-min call next week so we can map the exact traffic shape and confirm a recommended pilot configuration? Suggested times: Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we book the call: 

1) If we pick the Feature Pilot and then decide to downgrade to compact after week 4, what happens to the work we did around function-calling? Is there a data or configuration migration cost?
2) Pilot discount: you mentioned 15% — is that fixed or negotiable? We may ask procurement to request a 20% pilot concession if we agree to a 6-month committed plan afterwards.
3) SLA & credits: if latency or uptime targets are missed during the pilot, what remedies are available? Are pilot customers eligible for formal SLA credits or only post-commitment?
4) Can you confirm whether the reserved capacity conversion applies to pilot consumption credits pro-rata, or do we need to re-purchase at committed pricing?

We want to avoid surprises for our product and procurement teams — happy to take a 30-min call. I'm available Wed 12/2 between 10–11am ET or Thu 12/3 after 2pm ET.

Team — forwarding Emma's clarifying questions and my proposed responses below. I updated the pricing calc and added a short clause we can offer as an exec exception for this pilot. Please review and ack so I can send to Emma + procurement tomorrow morning.

Quick proposed responses (draft):
- Downgrade & feature migration: function-calling configuration is preserved at the user/meta level; model variant downgrade requires a short conversion window where inference configs are re-pointed. No mandatory rework from the customer side for typical setups; optional migration assistance is billable at standard SOW rates if they want Redwood to perform the conversion.
- Pilot discount: approve up to 20% as a one-time concession for a 6-week pilot if Sparrow signs an LOI to a 3–6 month reserved commitment within 30 days of pilot close. (Asking for gen approval here.)
- SLA & credits during pilot: Customers on a pilot are covered by an operational SLA baseline (internal SLO targets) but formal contractual SLA credits apply only once a Reserved (Committed) contract is executed. For pilots, we offer service credits (one-time credit toward committed purchase) as a goodwill remedy — not automatic contractual credits.
- Conversion of pilot credits: pilot prepaid credits can be applied pro-rata toward a reserved capacity purchase; if reserved pricing is lower, we credit the difference as an account-level credit for future invoices (not a refund).

Attachments: tier-pricing-calc.xlsx (v2) — I adjusted the seat vs throughput lines and modeled the 20% concession.

Action items:
- Kim: confirm the downgrade/migration language (especially anything that would require security review for PHI data flow changes).
- Mateo: if you're comfortable with the 20% pilot concession, please approve and I'll include the exec exception clause in my reply to procurement.

Thanks,
Ben
